summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize's quantization playground comparing INT8 and FP8 profiles for latency-sensitive inference routes; agreed pilot scope to run sandboxed benchmarks on Peregrine's eval sets and define rollback/fallback rules.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kulkarni (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood PM); Marta Ruiz (CTO, Peregrine Labs), Andy Park (ML Engineer), Samir Khan (Head Infra), Rosa Diaz (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya who will run the Optimize playground demo.
[00:10] Marta: Hi thanks, we are excited — short context, Peregrine runs a real-time docs summarization service, latency target is p95 < 150ms for our low-latency route, quality can't drop more than ~2% on our custom eval.
[00:28] Priya: great — we'll show the Console Optimize qprofile playground, comparisons between INT8 and FP8 profiles, and how to set adaptive fallback rules. we'll also propose a sandbox pilot.
[00:45] Andy: quick question — are you able to run our evals in the hosted sandbox or do we need private? we have some PHI-ish examples but most are synthetic.
[00:55] Jordan: good call — for the pilot we can run in Redwood hosted sandbox with redacted inputs; if you need on-prem/VPC we'll include Private in the contract but initial bench can be hosted.

[03:12] Priya: opening the Optimize console — note the qprofile gallery on the left, we're going to pick two profiles: an FP8 "fidelity-first" profile and an INT8 "speed-first" profile, then run batch evals and a latency-sensitive live route. please excuse the screenshot OCR sometimes reads it weird.
[03:46] Priya: baseline model here is an Llama-variant we've onboarded, with typical sequence length ~200 tokens for your use case. expected token generation per request ~120 tokens.

[06:05] Speaker 1 (Priya, sometimes labeled Speaker 1): starting the quant sweep — first run: FP8 profile with mixed-math kernels, no activations folding. warm cache run — p95 observed ~95ms, median ~40ms, cost per 1k tokens approx $1.8 in hosted.
[06:32] Speaker 2 (Andy / Customer): sorry did you say ninety five ms p95? that seems lower than we expected.
[06:40] Priya: yes for that profile, because FP8 keeps more numeric fidelity so we can run smaller kernel tiling and get better throughput without hitting large quality regressions.

[09:00] Priya: next run INT8 aggressive profile — more quantization, smaller memory footprint, we see p95 ~72ms, median ~30ms, cost per 1k tokens ~$1.1. quality delta on our quick eval was ~2.8% perplexity increase and some edge-case hallucinations on rare entity types.
[09:30] Marta: hm 2.8% exceeds our tolerance, can you show example regressions?
[09:38] Priya: pulled two diff examples in the console — quotex mislabel on a drug entity, and a subtle instruction-following issue. Important to note: those were on cold-cache; with prompt-rewrite and prefix KV-cache we can mitigate many of these.

[12:05] Priya: switching to the adaptive fallback rules panel — you can set per-route thresholds: for example, prefer INT8 for latency-critical route unless quality metric (BLEU/EM/your custom score) drops >1.5% on a rolling window, then fallback to FP8. we show simulated rollouts: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback.
[12:45] Rosa: how do we surface our custom metric? we run a composite score that weights factuality higher.
[12:55] Priya: you can push your evals to our evals endpoint (we'll provide a small script). Optimize ingests your metric and shows live delta versus baseline. we map it to a single numeric threshold for fallback rules.

[16:20] Liam: note on runtime — we do automatic kernel selection based on sequence length distribution; if your route has long tails >512 tokens, the performance shapes change and INT8 may not give as much benefit. also, batching behavior and continuous batching settings are adjustable per route.
[16:48] Samir: network question — if we run hosted, will p95 be impacted by cross-region hops? our infra uses eu-west-1 primarily.
[16:58] Jordan: we match region to reduce network RTT; hosted sandbox will be eu-west-1; for production you can use Dedicated in that region or Private VPC. cross-region fallback policies are possible but will add latency.

[21:10] Priya: live demo of an interactive trace — the console shows token-by-token latency heatmap, contribution of KV cache hits reduce latency by ~25% in that run, which closed some of the quality gaps at similar latency.
[21:40] Andy: can we tune quantization table for a specific token subspace? for example, clinical terminology we want higher precision on.
[21:52] Priya: yes via selective fidelity: we support token-level prefix locking and partial higher-precision layers (selective dequant). it's advanced but works; we can include an example qprofile that keeps embeddings for a named-entity class in higher precision.

[25:05] Marta: operationally, how do we detect that quality drift is from quantization vs a model update?
[25:15] Priya: Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets and to explicit deployments — we snapshot qprofiles and model checkpoints; if the delta aligns with a model upgrade we flag model change. we'll also surface per-deployment token distributions and a bucketed regression heatmap.

[29:40] Andy: what about rollback time — if we detect regression at 10% traffic, how fast can we flip to FP8?
[29:48] Priya: typically rollout/fallback is sub-second from the control plane to serving (we orchestrate routing rules). cold-starts might add a few 100ms for the warmup, but we keep a warm standby for quick swaps if you require immediate rollback.

[33:00] Priya: cost economics slide — example: for your traffic shape, switching to INT8 saves ~38% token cost but costs you ~2.5% quality delta if left unchecked; FP8 sits between cost and fidelity. we recommend a hybrid: INT8 for net-new low-risk routes, FP8 for high-fact routes, and adaptive fallback on the critical route.

[36:20] Rosa: timeline — we need to get this into a pilot and then to production within Q3. what's a realistic pilot that shows value?
[36:30] Jordan: 3-week sandbox pilot: week 1 onboarding + eval ingestion, week 2 benchmark runs with qprofile sweep, week 3 production-mirroring test and runbook validation. deliverables: benchmark report, recommended qprofiles, fallback rules, pilot pricing.

[40:00] Priya: demo: we create two sample qprofiles in the playground and run both through your uploaded eval set. ill show the difference report — note the "fidelity regression matrix" and per-prompt highlights.
[40:30] (short silence, typing noises)
[42:05] Andy: some fillers in the transcription — that first sample regression shows wrong dosage units, that's a blocker.
[42:18] Priya: yes, that's why we flagged it. for those entity-sensitive cases we can create a target override: always run FP8 or FP16 for prompts matching a regex, or route to a dedicated model variant.

[45:20] Marta: anything else we should be aware of on the security/compliance side for the hosted sandbox?
[45:28] Jordan: sandbox is ephemeral, logs retained short-term; for production we support SOC2 controls, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key management, and audit trails — i will attach the security binder.

[48:10] Samir: network egress — any special ports or peering required if we sample live traffic?
[48:20] Priya: no special ports; for Private deployments we'll do VPC peering and private IPs. for hosted benchmarks we'll request an allowlist for our test IPs if you prefer.

[51:00] Jordan: quick price note — pilot discounts available; production pricing will be per-token with a qprofile multiplier ranges and options for reserved Dedicated capacity if throughput required.
[52:20] Rosa: how do we measure user-perceived latency vs token-level latency so we can present to PMs?
[52:30] Priya: Optimize provides route-level p50/p95/p99 plus end-to-end measured RTT if you include client-side beaconing; we'll provide a short snippet to add to your frontend.

[55:10] Jordan: recap and next steps — Jordan will send pricing and contract template; Priya will provision sandbox and two sample qprofiles for Peregrine and run an initial sweep; Andy will upload evals; Samir will confirm region and network. we'll reconvene for benchmark review the week of June 23rd.
[55:45] Marta: sounds good, thanks all.
[55:52] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the security binder. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mis-attribution (Speaker 1/2), imperfect proper nouns (some drug names may be garbled), timestamps approximate.
